goals: Mechanistic/characterization: quantify how modeled peak SWE varies along the Wenatchee elevation gradient
Validation: assess model peak-SWE skill against the 5 in-basin SNOTEL stations
drivers_to_resolve: elevation (acting through NLDAS precipitation and temperature)

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM simulates SWE natively and NLDAS forcing varies orographically across this high-relief CONUS basin, so an elevation transect of columns plus SNOTEL-pinned validation columns answers both goals.

answerable: Peak SWE variation along the elevation gradient (NLDAS resolves precip/temp with elevation across ~2683 m relief)
SNOTEL peak-SWE validation (H2OSNO in default output; SNOTEL SWE available for 5 stations)

not_answerable.why: NLDAS 0.125° cells average over terrain; no within-cell lapse rate, so high exposed stations sit in cells with lower mean elevation

sampling_strategy.n_justification: Four elevation bands spanning the 187-2870 m gradient, ~2 columns per band. NLDAS resolves only ~12 distinct precip cells across this basin, so ~8 columns span the forcing contrast without redundant oversampling.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: West-to-east valley-to-crest transect: concentrate along the main elevation gradient and at the rain-snow transition (~1000-1800 m) where peak-SWE sensitivity to elevation is steepest.
sampling_strategy.replication: Light — 2 columns per band to check within-band spread from soil/aspect proxies; interannual replication via multi-winter run instead of duplicate columns.

sampling_plan.reason: Low-elevation, largely rain-dominated end-member; anchors the low end of the peak-SWE vs elevation curve.
Rain-snow transition zone where peak SWE is most sensitive to elevation/temperature; key gradient region.
Reliable seasonal snowpack band; overlaps typical SNOTEL siting for cross-checking exploratory vs validation columns.
Deep-snowpack high end-member; tests upper limb and expected 12 km ridgetop SWE underestimation.
Validation columns pinned to the 5 SNOTEL stations for co-located peak-SWE comparison; coordinates require a SNOTEL metadata resolver.

validation_design.comparison: co-located — extract each SNOTEL grid cell's annual peak SWE and compare to the station's observed annual peak; report per-station and pooled across water years 2010-2018
validation_design.metric: bias (expected negative at high stations), RMSE, and correlation of peak-SWE timing

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline NLDAS-2 forcing, native SSURGO soil, 1 lead-in year + 2010-2018 analysis winters

requires_capabilities.why: Brief lists 5 SNOTEL stations but no lat/lon; validation columns must be pinned to true station locations
requires_capabilities.blocks: placement of the 5 co-located validation columns

requires_capabilities.why: Needed to assign each column to an elevation band and to quantify the grid-cell-vs-station elevation offset driving ridgetop bias
requires_capabilities.blocks: labeling exploratory columns by band and interpreting SNOTEL bias

requires_capabilities.why: NLDAS 0.125° averages over terrain and lacks within-cell lapse rate
requires_capabilities.blocks: accurate high/ridgetop peak-SWE magnitudes (bias is reportable but not correctable in current stack)

requires_capabilities.why: Question asks for per-water-year peak SWE per column and at stations

assumptions: Peak SWE is a fast seasonal state; 1 lead-in year plus multiple analysis winters (2010-2018) is adequate spin-up — no multi-year hydrologic spin-up needed.
Exploratory column coordinates are placement intent along a valley-to-crest transect; true band membership must be confirmed via DEM lookup.
SNOTEL stations lie within the bbox and their cells are covered by NLDAS.
open_questions: What are the 5 SNOTEL station coordinates/elevations?
Should the analysis window (2010-2018) be extended earlier (1980+) to capture more interannual/climate variability, accepting ~10x NLDAS cost per added year per column?
Are aspect or vegetation contrasts of interest, or is elevation the sole axis to resolve?
